options: Email using the Notary Department's published address
An unsigned note left on a random desk
A comment under an unrelated website article
A message only to the affected signer
questions.explanation: The statute allows published-address email, certified mail, or another receipted delivery method.
feedback: Correct. The statute allows published-address email, certified mail, or another receipted delivery method.
That does not establish a listed delivery method.
That is not notice to the designated office.
The required recipient is the lieutenant governor.

questions.stem: A Utah notary authorizes a technician to repair journal-storage software. Which fact matters when assessing the statutory interference definition?
options: Every technical access is automatically unlawful
An invoice permits alteration of notarized facts
A repair appointment transfers ownership of every recording
Whether the technician has legal or granted technical-support authority
questions.explanation: The definition of authority includes specified notary-authorized maintenance, repair and technical support.
feedback: The chapter defines authority covering certain permitted support.
Technical support authority does not authorize falsifying records.
Support authorization does not transfer the notary's records.
Correct. The definition of authority includes specified notary-authorized maintenance, repair and technical support.

questions.stem: A Utah remote application supplies a name and bond but leaves the compliance agreement and email fields empty. What is incomplete?
options: Only a promise to advertise online
Nothing, because the vendor can answer all official notices
The required agreement to follow the chapter and rules and the applicant's email address
Only the future customer list
questions.explanation: The remote-application statute identifies both items.
feedback: Advertising is not the compliance agreement.
Vendor assistance does not remove the applicant's required information.
Correct. The remote-application statute identifies both items.
A customer list is not the omitted statutory application information.

questions.stem: A Utah applicant refuses the state-provided signed waiver needed for the statutory criminal-background review. Which application requirement remains unfinished?
options: Nothing, because a private employer already checked
The required background-check waiver
Only a journal purchase
Only a client consent form
questions.explanation: The code directs the office to require the specified signed waiver.
feedback: A private check does not replace the state's required process.
Correct. The code directs the office to require the specified signed waiver.
A journal does not replace the background-review waiver.
Client consent does not authorize the applicant's criminal-background process.

questions.stem: A Utah manager asks an employee-notary to deliberately violate a requirement of the notary chapter. What does the chapter specifically address?
options: An employer's solicitation of a chapter violation can be a class B misdemeanor
Only completed fraud can have consequences
A manager's request automatically authorizes the act
The notary must obey if overtime is paid
questions.explanation: The code expressly addresses employer solicitation, subject to its other-criminal-offense qualification.
feedback: Correct. The code expressly addresses employer solicitation, subject to its other-criminal-offense qualification.
The provision expressly reaches solicitation of a chapter violation.
Employment authority cannot override statute.
Extra pay does not authorize a statutory violation.

questions.stem: The Utah office learns that a commissioned notary now has a ground that would justify denial of an application. What disciplinary authority is stated?
options: Only a customer may cancel the commission
The commission must continue unchanged until expiration
A vendor can extend the commission instead
The lieutenant governor may revoke or suspend the commission
questions.explanation: The code ties revocation or suspension grounds to application-denial grounds.
feedback: The statutory authority belongs to the lieutenant governor.
The chapter authorizes discipline during the term.
A vendor cannot extend state authority.
Correct. The code ties revocation or suspension grounds to application-denial grounds.

questions.stem: A Utah notarization violates the notary chapter. A question arises specifically about statutory notice to third parties of the document's contents. What narrow rule applies?
options: The violation is forgiven for discipline purposes
The notary may knowingly repeat the violation
The violation does not by itself invalidate that notice
Every aspect of the transaction is automatically valid
questions.explanation: The section preserves this limited notice effect despite a chapter violation.
feedback: The notice rule does not eliminate the notary's statutory duties.
The notice provision does not authorize misconduct.
Correct. The section preserves this limited notice effect despite a chapter violation.
The section speaks narrowly to notice rather than universal validity.

questions.stem: A Utah applicant argues that passing the examination compels approval despite documented prior official notarial misconduct. What authority does the statute provide?
options: Only convictions can ever support denial
The lieutenant governor may deny an application on the listed grounds
Every passing score guarantees approval
Only the vendor may examine misconduct
questions.explanation: Passing the test does not erase the chapter's separate denial grounds.
feedback: The listed grounds also include official misconduct and specified license actions.
Correct. Passing the test does not erase the chapter's separate denial grounds.
The statute authorizes denial for additional grounds.
The denial authority belongs to the lieutenant governor.

questions.stem: A Utah RON certification starts late in an ordinary term. What period must the additional bond cover?
options: From the remote certification's effective date to the ordinary commission's expiration
A new four-year period beyond ordinary expiration
Only the first customer appointment
Only the vendor's subscription month
questions.explanation: The code specifies this beginning and ending for the additional coverage.
feedback: Correct. The code specifies this beginning and ending for the additional coverage.
The additional bond ends with the commission.
Coverage is not limited to one appointment.
The statutory period follows certification and commission dates.

questions.stem: A Utah notary examines the electronic-message certificate completion provision. Which information set does that provision identify electronically?
options: Only a company logo
Only the customer's electronic signature
Only an unverified typed nickname
Exact commissioned name and number with notary-public, Utah and expiration wording
questions.explanation: The electronic-message provision lists these electronic details; other applicable electronic or remote requirements must also be checked.
feedback: The provision specifies commission information.
The customer's signature does not supply the notary details.
The name and number must match the commission.
Correct. The electronic-message provision lists these electronic details; other applicable electronic or remote requirements must also be checked.

questions.stem: A Utah remote-certification application lists a nickname different from the ordinary commission record. What name rule should be followed?
options: Use the first customer's name
Leave the name blank until the first remote act
Use the name as it appears on the commission
Use any brand name chosen by the vendor
questions.explanation: The remote application must identify the applicant by the commissioned name.
feedback: The applicant is the notary, not the customer.
A properly completed application requires the applicant's name.
Correct. The remote application must identify the applicant by the commissioned name.
Branding does not replace the commissioned identity.

questions.stem: A Utah notary obtains the additional remote bond and uploads it. Before that bond becomes effective for remote authority, whose approval is required?
options: No approval once a credit card is charged
The lieutenant governor's approval
Only the signer's approval
Only a seal vendor's advertisement review
questions.explanation: The remote bond must be approved by the lieutenant governor before becoming effective.
feedback: Purchase alone does not replace official approval.
Correct. The remote bond must be approved by the lieutenant governor before becoming effective.
A customer cannot approve the statutory bond.
Advertising review is unrelated to bond approval.

cards.title: Commission continuity
cards.front: What connection to Utah supports an application?
cards.rule: Lawful Utah residence or Utah employment for at least thirty days precedes the application.
cards.boundary: The qualifying connection must continue during the term.
cards.mixup: A mailing address alone does not establish the stated qualification.

cards.title: Term calendar
cards.front: How long does ordinary Utah authority last?
cards.rule: The ordinary commission has a four-year term.
cards.boundary: Expired authority requires a new commission before further acts.
cards.mixup: A pending application does not extend an expired term.

cards.title: Disclosure completeness
cards.front: Which professional history belongs on the application?
cards.rule: Disclose required criminal history and actions concerning notarial or other professional licenses.
cards.boundary: The statute reaches relevant history beyond Utah.
cards.mixup: A dismissed assumption about relevance can leave an application incomplete.

cards.title: Background sequence
cards.front: Should bond preparation stop pending a background-result email?
cards.rule: The current process instructs applicants to continue to bond and oath preparation without waiting for results.
cards.boundary: The office says it does not separately notify applicants of processing.
cards.mixup: Silence does not mean the application is ready for notarizations.
cards.source: Utah Process and Qualifications, background check

cards.title: Bond identity
cards.front: What must the bond name match?
cards.rule: The bond name must match the notary application, and the applicant signs as principal.
cards.boundary: A purchased unsigned bond does not finish this step.
cards.mixup: The surety's signature does not replace the principal's signature.

cards.title: Official-name signature
cards.front: Which name is signed on a notarial certificate?
cards.rule: Sign exactly and only the name indicated on the commission.
cards.boundary: Personal shorthand does not change the commissioned record.
cards.mixup: The company name cannot replace the commissioned individual's signature.

cards.title: Physical seal design
cards.front: What makes Utah's ink seal suitable?
cards.rule: It must be sharp, legible, photographically reproducible and contain the required commission details within the specified rectangular border.
cards.boundary: The maximum border is one inch by two and one-half inches.
cards.mixup: An embosser alone does not replace this seal.

cards.title: Name-change file
cards.front: What accompanies the changed official name?
cards.rule: Supply official name-change documentation and the bond policy rider within thirty days.
cards.boundary: The rider reflects the old and new names.
cards.mixup: Marriage itself does not require adoption of the spouse's surname.

cards.title: Impartial service
cards.front: How should a notary approach a lawful requested act?
cards.rule: The chapter requires performance of a lawful act for a requesting person who tenders the appropriate fee.
cards.boundary: The notary must still satisfy all applicable legal requirements.
cards.mixup: Personal influence over whether to enter a lawful transaction is restricted.

cards.title: Financial interest screen
cards.front: When does a financial role create disqualification?
cards.rule: The statute restricts notarizing when the notary has the specified direct financial or property interests.
cards.boundary: Narrow escrow, title-producer and attorney-role provisions require their actual conditions.
cards.mixup: Being employed by a business does not answer every conflict question.

cards.title: Acknowledgment admission
cards.front: What does an acknowledgment establish?
cards.rule: The identified appearing person admits voluntary execution for the stated purpose.
cards.boundary: An earlier signature can be acknowledged through a present appearance.
cards.mixup: An old signature alone does not establish today's acknowledgment.

cards.title: Jurat sequence
cards.front: What belongs before witnessing a jurat signature?
cards.rule: Administer the oath or affirmation and then witness the voluntary signature.
cards.boundary: The signer must be identified through an applicable route.
cards.mixup: A signature acknowledgment does not supply a truthfulness oath.

cards.title: Affirmation choice
cards.front: How can a signer undertake truthfulness without a religious oath?
cards.rule: Use an affirmation that solemnly declares the truth of the statements.
cards.boundary: The notary must actually administer the required commitment.
cards.mixup: Silently handing over the paper does not administer an affirmation.

cards.title: Signature witnessing
cards.front: What is observed during signature witnessing?
cards.rule: The identified person voluntarily signs in the notary's presence.
cards.boundary: A truthfulness oath belongs to a different act when required.
cards.mixup: An existing signature does not satisfy the witnessing definition by itself.

cards.title: Personal knowledge threshold
cards.front: What qualifies as personal knowledge of identity?
cards.rule: Interactions must provide sufficient acquaintance to eliminate every reasonable doubt about identity.
cards.boundary: Familiar appearance alone may leave reasonable doubt.
cards.mixup: Coworker status is not an automatic substitute for sufficient knowledge.

cards.title: Government identification
cards.front: What features belong to the standard government-ID route?
cards.rule: The qualifying unexpired identification includes the required photograph, signature and physical description.
cards.boundary: The code separately recognizes an unexpired passport from any nation.
cards.mixup: A driving privilege card is expressly excluded.

cards.title: Known credible individual
cards.front: What connects a personally known credible witness to the signer?
cards.rule: The credible individual knows the principal and supplies the required sworn verification.
cards.boundary: The notary's personal knowledge of the witness is part of this route.
cards.mixup: The witness's confidence without the oath leaves a required step undone.

cards.title: Unknown credible individual
cards.front: Can a witness unknown to the notary ever be used?
cards.rule: The current code permits the specified route using the witness's qualifying identification and oath concerning the principal.
cards.boundary: Remote use adds the applicable secondary authentication.
cards.mixup: Merely introducing a stranger does not complete the route.

cards.title: Certificate truth
cards.front: What information can the notary certify?
cards.rule: The certificate must accurately describe the act actually performed.
cards.boundary: Knowingly false or materially incomplete certificates are prohibited.
cards.mixup: A customer's preferred date cannot replace the actual notarial event.

cards.title: Plat exception
cards.front: When can a paper map certificate omit the seal imprint?
cards.rule: The specific map-or-plat exception requires a permanent-ink signature and adjacent exact commission details and statutory Utah statement.
cards.boundary: The exception expressly excludes remote certificates.
cards.mixup: A small blank space alone does not create an exception.

cards.title: Eligible source record
cards.front: What records fit Utah's copy-certification definition?
cards.rule: The source must fall outside the public-record and publicly-recorded exclusions.
cards.boundary: Record status matters even when the photocopy is perfectly clear.
cards.mixup: A customer's ownership of a record does not remove the exclusion.

cards.title: Comparison purpose
cards.front: What does comparing the original and photocopy accomplish?
cards.rule: It supports the statement that the copy is accurate, exact and unaltered.
cards.boundary: Underlying factual claims remain outside the copy-comparison determination.
cards.mixup: Certifying a copy does not authenticate every assertion written in it.

cards.title: Missing-page boundary
cards.front: What happens if the proposed copy omits a page?
cards.rule: The notary cannot truthfully certify it as an exact copy of the complete source.
cards.boundary: Obtain an accurate reproduction before making the certification.
cards.mixup: A readable first page does not cure an omitted second page.

cards.title: Publicly recorded exclusion
cards.front: Does recording status affect a private customer's request?
cards.rule: A publicly recorded document is excluded from the statutory copy-certification definition.
cards.boundary: The requester's private use does not alter the document's status.
cards.mixup: A fee waiver cannot convert an excluded record into an eligible record.

cards.title: Copy certificate details
cards.front: What connects the certificate to the copied material?
cards.rule: The statutory form identifies or describes the document whose copy was compared.
cards.boundary: The notary must accurately identify the comparison performed.
cards.mixup: A generic seal impression does not describe the certified copy.

cards.title: Per-page ceiling
cards.front: How is the ordinary copy-certification fee limited?
cards.rule: The ordinary ceiling is ten dollars for each page certified.
cards.boundary: Remote fee provisions have a separate per-item rule.
cards.mixup: Counting the customer's signatures is not the copy-certification fee unit.

cards.title: Copy and signature acts
cards.front: Does a customer's signature establish copy accuracy?
cards.rule: A signature act and a copy certification have different statutory elements.
cards.boundary: Use the requested lawful act's actual procedure.
cards.mixup: Acknowledging a cover letter does not establish that an attachment is an exact copy.

cards.title: Certification confidence
cards.front: What should a notary do when reproduction quality hides content?
cards.rule: Resolve the comparison problem before certifying an exact and unaltered copy.
cards.boundary: The certificate must remain truthful.
cards.mixup: A larger fee does not supply missing comparison evidence.

cards.title: 2026 transition
cards.front: Which date triggers the new ordinary journal duty?
cards.rule: A commission issued on or after May 6, 2026 brings the new physical-journal requirement.
cards.boundary: The rule includes renewed commissions after that date.
cards.mixup: The date the journal was purchased does not determine the cohort.

cards.title: Paper and remote media
cards.front: Which record medium matches each act?
cards.rule: New-cohort nonremote acts go in a physical journal, while remote acts use a secure electronic journal.
cards.boundary: Remote status does not convert in-person acts into electronic-only entries.
cards.mixup: A spreadsheet is not the required bound physical journal.

cards.title: Entry timing
cards.front: When is the new-cohort journal entry made?
cards.rule: Record the required details at completion of the notarial act.
cards.boundary: The physical journal must be bound and chronological.
cards.mixup: An end-of-month summary does not satisfy completion-time entries.

cards.title: ID data minimization
cards.front: Which identification number detail is required in the new entry?
cards.rule: Record the last four digits together with type, issuer, issue date and expiration date.
cards.boundary: The rule does not call for writing the complete number in this field.
cards.mixup: A bare note saying 'ID checked' omits required details.

cards.title: Grouped entry boundary
cards.front: When can multiple acts share one entry?
cards.rule: The acts must involve the same individual at the same time on one record or similar records.
cards.boundary: Different individuals do not satisfy the grouped-entry rule.
cards.mixup: A shared employer alone does not authorize grouping unrelated appointments.

cards.title: Coworker signature exception
cards.front: What conditions support the limited repeated-signature exception?
cards.rule: The prior act within 180 days, personal knowledge, employer-or-coworker role, ordinary business transaction and required notation must all be present.
cards.boundary: This is an exception to the journal signature requirement.
cards.mixup: One condition by itself does not remove the entry requirements.

cards.title: Refusal record
cards.front: What should the journal preserve after a refusal?
cards.rule: Record obtainable required information and describe the reason for refusing or not completing the act.
cards.boundary: An uncompleted act can still require an entry.
cards.mixup: Deleting the appointment is not the required journal response.

cards.title: Ten-year clock
cards.front: What event starts the retention period?
cards.rule: Retain the journal for ten years after its last recorded notarial act.
cards.boundary: Leaving the profession does not shorten this retention period.
cards.mixup: The first page's date does not set the last-act clock.

cards.title: Specific-entry access
cards.front: What limits an ordinary inspection request?
cards.rule: The identified requester supplies the specified act, document, month and year, principal and signed request entry.
cards.boundary: Only the requested entry is exposed.
cards.mixup: An interest in one transaction does not authorize browsing unrelated entries.

cards.title: Protected remote identity data
cards.front: How are biometrics and ID images treated on release?
cards.rule: The protected portion needs the subject's written consent, a court order or the lieutenant governor's authorized request.
cards.boundary: General journal-access procedures do not erase this protection.
cards.mixup: A requester's curiosity is not a release ground.

cards.title: Employment exception
cards.front: Which workplace acts receive the stated journal exception?
cards.rule: Acts within the course and scope of employment by an attorney, law firm or title agency receive the statutory treatment.
cards.boundary: Unrelated personal acts fall outside that employment condition.
cards.mixup: An ordinary commercial employer is not automatically a title agency.

cards.title: Custody at departure
cards.front: Can an ordinary employer demand the journal when employment ends?
cards.rule: The chapter generally prohibits demanding surrender at termination.
cards.boundary: Apply the separate statutory attorney, law-firm and title-agency records provisions where relevant.
cards.mixup: Buying a notebook does not automatically grant an ordinary employer the journal.

cards.title: Separate certification
cards.front: What must ordinary Utah authority precede?
cards.rule: The published RON process requires an existing commission and separate remote approval.
cards.boundary: Remote approval must be reapplied for when renewing the ordinary commission.
cards.mixup: A video account does not itself create remote authority.

cards.title: Physical location
cards.front: Where must the Utah remote notary work?
cards.rule: The remote notary must be physically in Utah.
cards.boundary: The customer's mailing address does not relocate the notary.
cards.mixup: A Utah server is not a substitute for the notary's location.

cards.title: Secondary identity
cards.front: What additional authentication accompanies applicable remote evidence?
cards.rule: Use the statutory secondary-authentication requirement, including its application to the unknown credible-witness route.
cards.boundary: Knowledge-based or biometric methods must meet the statutory definitions and applicable rules.
cards.mixup: Passing identity authentication does not administer a jurat oath.

cards.title: Remote recording
cards.front: What record must the electronic journal include?
cards.rule: Include the remote audiovisual recording with the electronic journal.
cards.boundary: Secure the record and required backups against unauthorized access.
cards.mixup: A meeting invitation is not the session recording.

cards.title: Alteration evidence
cards.front: How must the signature and electronic seal be attached?
cards.rule: Attach them so that later changes to the certificate and associated electronic record become evident.
cards.boundary: A freely reusable picture alone does not establish that protection.
cards.mixup: Visual similarity to a stamp does not prove tamper evidence.

cards.title: Bond increase
cards.front: What coverage supports remote approval?
cards.rule: The process requires ten thousand dollars total coverage through a rider or additional five-thousand-dollar bond.
cards.boundary: Additional coverage follows the ordinary commission renewal cycle.
cards.mixup: A vendor subscription is not bond coverage.

cards.title: Seal guardian limits
cards.front: What may the electronic-seal guardian protect?
cards.rule: The provider can hold the seal under statutory access and purpose restrictions.
cards.boundary: Only the named remote notary uses it to perform notarizations.
cards.mixup: Custody does not permit another employee to act under that seal.

cards.title: End-of-authority credentials
cards.front: What happens to enabling remote credentials at expiration?
cards.rule: Destroy the listed enabling items and certify compliance to the lieutenant governor within ten days.
cards.boundary: The journal and recordings follow their separate retention duties.
cards.mixup: Credential destruction does not authorize premature deletion of records.

cards.title: Remote certificate statement
cards.front: What extra fact belongs in the remote certificate?
cards.rule: State that the notarization was performed remotely.
cards.boundary: All other applicable act and certificate requirements still apply.
cards.mixup: A vendor logo does not supply that statement.

cards.title: Approved workflow
cards.front: What completes the published RON application sequence?
cards.rule: Submit the listed oath, bond and seal sample, pay after instructions, and receive final active confirmation.
cards.boundary: Vendor setup alone is an earlier step.
cards.mixup: Document-review progress is not final authorization.

commission.summary: A Utah commission combines eligibility, an online examination, background review, bonding and a notarized oath. Its four-year authority carries continuing name, address, signature and seal duties.

sections.heading: Build a complete commission file
sections.body: The current process starts with qualifications and a state account, then the online test and payment. The office directs applicants to continue preparing the bond and oath while the background review proceeds. The bond name matches the application and the applicant signs as principal. Uploading the signed bond and notarized oath completes the application without a separate Final Submit button. Approval and the Certificate of Authority precede purchasing the official supplies.

sections.heading: Keep the authority usable
sections.body: Use the exact commissioned name for the official signature and obtain the compliant seal. A new commission requires a new seal. Report a residential or business address change within thirty days. A legal name change requires the documented state filing and bond rider procedure, including destruction of the former commission and seal. Check conflicts before each act and avoid using official office to promote a product or supply legal advice.

example.heading: Office move during a term
example.body: A Provo employee-notary changes business offices while keeping the same home. The business address change still has its own thirty-day notice requirement. The move does not create a new four-year term or eliminate the need to protect the personally assigned stamp.

keyFacts: Ordinary commissions run for four years.
The current first application process includes an online examination and mandatory background check.
The ordinary bond is five thousand dollars.
Use the exact commissioned name in the official signature.

acts.summary: Identify the requested act before performing it. Utah distinguishes acknowledgment, jurat, signature witnessing, oath or affirmation, and eligible copy certification.

sections.heading: Match the procedure to the certificate
sections.body: An acknowledgment establishes the appearing person's admission of voluntary execution and can concern an earlier signature. A jurat includes the truthfulness oath or affirmation and voluntary signing in the notary's presence. Signature witnessing also requires present signing but does not by itself include the truthfulness oath. Complete a certificate describing the actual act, including a remote statement when applicable.

sections.heading: Establish identity through an actual statutory route
sections.body: Personal knowledge requires enough acquaintance to eliminate every reasonable doubt. Otherwise apply a qualifying unexpired identification or credible-individual route. The current code permits both a credible witness personally known to the notary and a separately conditioned route for an unknown credible witness. Remote evidence adds its applicable secondary authentication. A driving privilege card does not qualify as satisfactory evidence under the stated exclusion.

example.heading: Already signed affidavit
example.body: At an Ogden appointment, a customer presents an affidavit with an earlier signature and a jurat. Explaining that acknowledgments can cover earlier signatures does not complete the requested jurat. The notary administers the oath or affirmation and witnesses the voluntary signing required for that act before making a truthful certificate.

keyFacts: An acknowledgment still requires appearance.
A jurat requires an oath or affirmation and present signing.
Signature witnessing has its own present-signing element.
An unknown credible witness must satisfy the current code's identification and oath conditions.

copies.summary: Utah copy certification addresses an accurate photocopy of an eligible source record. Public records and publicly recorded documents fall outside its statutory definition.

sections.heading: Screen the source before comparison
sections.body: Determine whether the requested source is eligible for the Utah copy-certification act. A customer's private purpose does not change a public record into a private record, and an exact image of a publicly recorded document remains outside the definition. Explain that the status of the source record controls this boundary before spending time comparing pages.

sections.heading: Certify the reproduction actually examined
sections.body: For an eligible source, compare the proposed photocopy and verify that it is accurate, exact and unaltered. A missing page, obscured content or changed text prevents that conclusion. Identify the source in the copy certificate and preserve a truthful description of the comparison. This act does not verify the factual truth of every statement in the source or guarantee its acceptance by a receiving organization.

example.heading: Two-page private certificate
example.body: A customer brings an eligible private two-page completion certificate with a photocopy containing only the first page. The notary requests a complete copy and compares both pages before considering certification. A separate acknowledgment on the customer's cover letter would establish a different act and would not establish the attachment's accuracy.

keyFacts: Screen for both public-record and publicly-recorded exclusions.
Compare the eligible source and the actual photocopy.
The ordinary copy-certification fee ceiling is ten dollars per page.
The certification concerns reproduction accuracy.

journal.summary: Utah's May 6, 2026 transition changes ordinary journal duties for newly issued and renewed commissions. Remote notaries also have secure electronic-journal and recording requirements.

sections.heading: Choose the cohort and medium
sections.body: A commission received on or after May 6, 2026 brings the new physical-journal duty for nonremote acts. The state supplement explicitly includes renewals after that date. The current code provides the bounded chronological physical format and completion-time entries. Remote acts use the secure electronic journal and associated audiovisual recording. Apply the limited employment exception for acts within the course and scope of qualifying attorney, law-firm or title-agency employment.

sections.heading: Retain securely and disclose carefully
sections.body: Preserve the journal for ten years after the last recorded act even after leaving the profession, then follow the statutory destruction requirements. Ordinary access is limited to a specified entry, an identified requester and a signed inspection-request entry containing the required details. Official requests have their own scope limitations. Remote biometric information and identification images have an additional written-consent, court-order or lieutenant-governor release restriction.

example.heading: Renewal changes the workflow
example.body: A notary whose prior commission predates the change renews in September 2026. Nonremote work under the renewed commission belongs in the required physical journal. The notary records the obtainable information and reason when refusing an incomplete appointment, instead of treating an unsuccessful meeting as having no record duty.

keyFacts: The transition is based on commission issuance, including renewal.
New-cohort entries include last four ID digits plus other specified ID details.
A limited multi-act entry needs the same person, same time and one or similar records.
Retention runs ten years from the last recorded act.

remote.summary: Utah RON requires a separate approved workflow, increased bond coverage and secure electronic execution. The remote notary performs the act while physically in Utah.

sections.heading: Obtain and maintain separate remote approval
sections.body: The published RON process requires an existing ordinary commission, hiring or contracting by an approved vendor, total bond coverage of ten thousand dollars and a vendor-provided electronic signature and seal. Submit the notarized remote oath, bond evidence and seal sample. The office sends separate fee instructions after document review, and final active confirmation completes approval. Reapply for remote authority when renewing the ordinary commission.

sections.heading: Conduct and preserve the remote act
sections.body: Meet the real-time communication and identity requirements, including applicable secondary authentication. Record the session and include the recording with the secure electronic journal. Render the remote seal in black and attach signature and seal so later alteration of the certificate or associated record is evident. Protect backups and apply the statutory restrictions to any vendor acting as seal guardian or journal custodian.

example.heading: Travel interrupts availability
example.body: A certified Utah remote notary visits Wyoming and receives a request from a Utah customer. A Utah vendor account and a Utah customer do not place the notary inside Utah. The notary arranges a session when physically back within the authorized state and still follows identity, act, certificate and recording requirements.

keyFacts: The remote notary must be physically in Utah.
Total RON bond coverage is ten thousand dollars.
Remote approval is reapplied for after ordinary renewal.
Remote certificates state that the act was performed remotely.

articles.keyword: A Utah renewal can change the journal workflow
articles.title: A Utah renewal can change the journal workflow
articles.description: Follow the commission-date transition through a practical office renewal.
articles.h1: A Utah renewal can change the journal workflow
articles.lede: A renewal in 2026 can bring a physical-journal duty that did not apply during the prior ordinary commission.

sections.heading: Read the issuance date
sections.body: A Salt Lake City notary has an ordinary commission issued in 2023 and renews it in September 2026. The operative event for the new journal cohort is receipt of a commission on or after May 6, 2026. The state supplement specifically includes renewed commissions, so the date the person first became a notary does not permanently fix the applicable ordinary journal treatment.

sections.heading: Assign a medium to each act
sections.body: Under the renewed commission, the required physical journal serves nonremote notarizations. The code calls for a bound, chronological journal and recording at completion of the act. If the same person also holds remote certification, remote acts go in the secure electronic journal with their audiovisual recording. A vendor account does not convert an office appointment into a remote act.

sections.heading: Carry the full entry forward
sections.body: The new entry captures the date and time, act type, document description, applicable identity evidence, oath indication when relevant, signer information and fee. The identification-card route includes the last four digits with the type, issuer, issuance and expiration dates. A habit of writing only a customer name and the phrase ID checked leaves important required fields absent.

sections.heading: Preserve the record after retirement
sections.body: The ten-year retention period runs from the last recorded notarial act, including when the individual is no longer a notary. At the end of the statutory period, the destruction requirements apply. Keeping a commission calendar beside the journal procedures helps an office identify the transition while maintaining the distinct retention clock for records already created.

faqs.q: Does renewing after May 6, 2026 count?
faqs.a: Yes. The official supplement expressly includes renewals after that date.

faqs.q: Can retirement shorten the retention period?
faqs.a: No. The statutory ten-year period continues after the person ceases acting as a notary.

articles.keyword: Using a credible individual in Utah
articles.title: Using a credible individual in Utah
articles.description: Distinguish the known-witness and unknown-witness routes before an appointment.
articles.h1: Using a credible individual in Utah
articles.lede: The current code provides more than one credible-individual route, each with its own evidence conditions.

sections.heading: Start with the relationship
sections.body: At a Logan office, a customer arrives without a qualifying identification document and brings a neighbor. The notary first determines whether the relevant statutory credible-individual route can actually be completed. A friendly introduction by itself does not establish personal knowledge of either person, and the witness must know the principal under the applicable route.

sections.heading: Use the known-witness route accurately
sections.body: One route involves a credible individual personally known to the notary who personally knows the principal and supplies the required sworn verification. Personal knowledge has a demanding statutory definition based on interactions sufficient to eliminate every reasonable doubt. The notary should assess the actual relationship and administer the required oath rather than rely on the witness merely saying that everything is fine.

sections.heading: Recognize the current additional route
sections.body: The current chapter separately permits a credible individual whom the notary does not personally know when the individual knows the principal, presents the qualifying identification and supplies the prescribed oath. A notary applying an older habit of requiring personal knowledge of every witness would overlook this distinct route. Its conditions must still be satisfied together before using it.

sections.heading: Apply the remote additions and record
sections.body: For the applicable remote route, the unknown credible individual also undergoes secondary authentication. The new-cohort journal specifies the oath indication, signature, witness name and address, with the relevant identification details for the unknown-witness route. Completing one identity component does not administer the principal's jurat oath or replace the other requirements of the requested act.

faqs.q: Must every credible individual be personally known to the notary?
faqs.a: The current code includes a separate route for an unknown credible individual with the specified identification and oath conditions.

faqs.q: Does a witness introduction itself complete identity verification?
faqs.a: No. Complete the actual statutory relationship, evidence and oath requirements.

articles.keyword: Responding to a Utah journal-entry request
articles.title: Responding to a Utah journal-entry request
articles.description: Keep the requested entry accessible while applying the statutory release boundaries.
articles.h1: Responding to a Utah journal-entry request
articles.lede: An ordinary inspection request concerns a specified act and requires its own journal entry.

sections.heading: Identify the request precisely
sections.body: An individual asks a Provo notary for a copy of an entry relating to a property transaction. During normal business hours, the ordinary request route requires that the notary know the requester personally or verify identity by satisfactory evidence. The requester also specifies the act type, document, month and year, and principal so the request can be tied to an actual entry.

sections.heading: Create the access record
sections.body: The requester signs a separate journal entry containing the name and address, identification method, requested notarial record, inspection or request date and reason. The notary then exposes only the specified entry. Opening a bound book to a page with other customers' details requires care so that fulfilling one request does not become an opportunity to browse unrelated transactions.

sections.heading: Separate official requests
sections.body: A law-enforcement request relating to an investigation, subpoena or court order follows the code's official-request provisions. Compliance is limited to the investigation's scope or the extent expressly stated in the subpoena or order. The chapter also permits refusal of an ordinary request when the notary has a reasonable, articulable belief of criminal or other harmful intent.

sections.heading: Protect the especially sensitive portion
sections.body: A remote recording may contain biometrics or an identification image. Releasing that portion requires the subject's written consent, an order from a court with jurisdiction, or a request by the lieutenant governor or designee. Ordinary access eligibility does not eliminate this additional restriction. Journals and remote recordings also have their expressly stated treatment outside the Government Records Access and Management Act.

faqs.q: May an ordinary requester browse the whole journal?
faqs.a: The ordinary route limits access to the specific entry requested.

faqs.q: Does a general inspection request automatically release an ID image?
faqs.a: No. The code supplies additional grounds for release of that protected portion.

articles.title: The Utah title-agency employment exception
articles.description: Apply the work-related journal exception to its stated employment context.
articles.lede: The code gives particular treatment to acts performed within specified legal and title employment.

sections.heading: Locate the employment condition
sections.body: A notary employed by a Utah title agency completes notarizations as part of closing work. The journal provision has a specific exception for acts within the course and scope of employment by an attorney, law firm or title agency. This calls for identifying the actual employer and work context before treating an act as covered by that exception.

sections.heading: Keep personal appointments distinct
sections.body: The same employee later helps a neighbor with an unrelated private document outside the title-agency work. Being employed by a title agency does not automatically put every personal appointment inside the course and scope of that employment. The notary applies the journal rules that govern the personal act, including the commission-date transition and any applicable remote duties.

sections.heading: Read the records treatment
sections.body: For acts within the stated employment setting, the statute addresses ownership and disclosure of the associated records and preserves the relevant attorney privilege. Those provisions should be read together with the exception. The general rule preventing an employer from demanding surrender at termination cannot be applied without considering the separate statutory treatment of these particular employment records.

sections.heading: Continue the other notarial duties
sections.body: A journal exception does not eliminate identity, appearance, certificate, impartiality or seal requirements. A title producer facing a possible conflict must separately examine the narrow provisions of the conflict section and the individual role in the transaction. An office can keep its work classification and certificate procedure clear without assuming that one exception resolves every notarial requirement.

faqs.q: Does any commercial employer qualify?
faqs.a: The provision identifies attorney, law-firm and title-agency employment, subject to its work-related conditions.

faqs.q: Does the exception waive identity checks?
faqs.a: No. Identity and the other requirements of the act still apply.

articles.keyword: Reporting a Utah seal or recording incident
articles.title: Reporting a Utah seal or recording incident
articles.description: Distinguish an interference discovery from accidental loss while preparing the required notice.
articles.h1: Reporting a Utah seal or recording incident
articles.lede: The 2026 chapter addresses both unlawful interference and discovery of lost, damaged or destroyed notarial items.

sections.heading: Identify the affected item
sections.body: An employee notices that a Utah notary's seal has disappeared and an unauthorized journal change has been made. The current chapter lists signatures, certificates, seals, notarial equipment, journals and remote recordings among the protected items. Knowing unauthorized use, access, concealment or alteration can fall within unlawful interference, so the response should account for the actual facts discovered.

sections.heading: Send the interference notices
sections.body: When discovering unlawful interference affecting the notary or items under the notary's custody or control, the notary immediately notifies law enforcement with jurisdiction and provides written notice to the lieutenant governor. Telling a supervisor can help office coordination, but that internal conversation does not supply either of the recipients specified by the statute.

sections.heading: Report accidental loss too
sections.body: A fire destroys a seal without evidence of unauthorized conduct. The separate discovery provision still requires immediate written notice to the lieutenant governor when a listed item is lost, damaged or destroyed. The notary does not need to wait for proof of a forged document before making this notice. A replacement stamp order is a different task and does not fulfill the state notice duty.

sections.heading: Include useful statutory details
sections.body: The written notice identifies the notary, address and commission number and describes the discovery and relevant facts. For an affected journal or recording, include the covered time period. An interference notice includes information enabling the office to identify and obtain the police report. Use the published office email, certified mail or another delivery method supplying a receipt as the statute permits.

faqs.q: Does accidental destruction require notice?
faqs.a: Yes. The separate loss, damage or destruction provision requires immediate written notice to the lieutenant governor.

faqs.q: Is notifying an employer sufficient after interference?
faqs.a: No. The statute specifies law enforcement with jurisdiction and written notice to the lieutenant governor.

articles.title: Screening a Utah copy-certification request
articles.description: Resolve the source-record boundary before comparing the pages.
articles.lede: A clear photocopy and an eligible source record are separate conditions in Utah copy certification.

sections.heading: Examine what the source is
sections.body: A customer brings a recorded deed to an Ogden notary and asks for a certified photocopy for private use. The Utah definition excludes public records and publicly recorded documents. The purpose of the proposed copy does not alter that source status, so an exact comparison alone cannot make this record eligible for the statutory copy-certification act.

sections.heading: Compare an eligible reproduction
sections.body: Another customer brings an eligible privately held course certificate. The notary compares the proposed photocopy with the source, checking that the material is accurate, exact and unaltered. If the source contains an additional page or legible information missing from the reproduction, the notary resolves that deficiency before making the prescribed certification.

sections.heading: Describe the narrow determination
sections.body: The copy certificate identifies or describes the document compared and addresses the reproduction. It does not establish that the course had regulatory approval or that the claims printed in the source are true. A receiving organization can have its own requirements, and the notary should keep the certificate limited to the comparison actually performed under Utah law.

sections.heading: Avoid substituting another act silently
sections.body: A customer may ask whether signing a statement about the copy would be a different option. Explain the procedural differences neutrally and keep any requested act and certificate truthful. An acknowledgment on a cover letter establishes the signer's acknowledgment, and cannot be described as the notary's comparison of the attached copy unless that separate eligible act was actually performed.

faqs.q: Does private use make a recorded document eligible?
faqs.a: No. The source-record exclusion still applies.

faqs.q: Does copy certification prove the source's factual claims?
faqs.a: It certifies the reproduction under the statutory procedure, rather than the underlying assertions.

articles.keyword: Utah plat certificates and the seal exception
articles.title: Utah plat certificates and the seal exception
articles.description: Use the map-or-plat provision only with its specified facts and information.
articles.h1: Utah plat certificates and the seal exception
articles.lede: A particular paper plat certificate has a limited completion rule that requires exact adjacent commission details.

sections.heading: Identify the applicable certificate
sections.body: A surveyor presents an in-person subdivision plat certificate with little room for a stamp. The chapter contains a special rule for annexation, subdivision or other maps or plats. Start by identifying that actual record and certificate instead of treating an inconvenient blank space on any document as a reason to omit a required seal imprint.

sections.heading: Supply every substitute detail
sections.body: The notary signs the certificate in permanent ink. Below or immediately adjacent to that signature appear the name and commission number exactly as shown on the commission, the statutory statement that the person is a notary public commissioned in Utah, and the commission expiration date. Those particular details are the condition for the stated no-imprint treatment.

sections.heading: Keep the underlying act complete
sections.body: The plat provision addresses certificate completion without the seal imprint under its conditions. It does not replace the appearing person's identity verification, the actual acknowledgment or other requested act, the accurate certificate date, or an applicable journal entry. The notary should still assess conflicts arising from any individual property interest in the transaction.

sections.heading: Check the remote exclusion
sections.body: The provision expressly excludes a certificate completed as part of remote notarization. A remote notary therefore cannot rely on the paper plat rule to omit the electronic seal. The remote signature and seal must satisfy their applicable attachment and alteration-evidence requirements even when the electronic record depicts a map, survey or subdivision boundary.

faqs.q: Does a cramped ordinary contract receive this exception?
faqs.a: The provision concerns the specified map-or-plat certificates with all stated conditions.

faqs.q: Can a RON plat certificate use the same no-imprint rule?
faqs.a: No. The provision expressly excludes remote certificates.

articles.keyword: Controlling Utah remote seals and records
articles.title: Controlling Utah remote seals and records
articles.description: Examine a vendor arrangement through the separate seal and journal provisions.
articles.h1: Controlling Utah remote seals and records
articles.lede: A Utah vendor may supply technology while the code imposes particular limits on access and use.

sections.heading: Review seal guardianship
sections.body: A certified remote notary uses a vendor that stores the electronic seal. The code permits a supplying person to act as guardian under statutory restrictions. The guardian secures access to the named remote notary and guardian, and prevents another person from using that seal to perform notarizations. A support employee does not acquire the notary's authority through possession of the technology.

sections.heading: Distinguish permitted technical purposes
sections.body: The guardian provisions allow narrow access or use related solely to completing the named notary's notarization, obtaining, storing or protecting the seal, or complying with a court order. These purposes are different from a provider performing a new act under the notary's name. A service contract should reflect the particular legal restrictions that apply to the vendor's role.

sections.heading: Read electronic-journal custody separately
sections.body: The remote journal and recordings have their own custodian framework. A designated custodian agreement must cover statutory safety, security, retention and destruction. The repository access exceptions are restricted to the specified completion, retention and court-order purposes. The notary also maintains and protects the required backups, preserving secure and authentic records of completed remote acts.

sections.heading: Plan for the term ending
sections.body: At expiration, resignation or revocation, destroy the listed credentials that enable use of the electronic signature or seal and provide the required ten-day written certification to the lieutenant governor. Records follow the separate journal-retention rules. Closing an account must therefore address both disabling future notarizations and preserving the records whose statutory retention period continues.

faqs.q: May a vendor employee notarize with the named notary's seal?
faqs.a: Only the named remote notary may use that seal to perform notarizations.

faqs.q: Does credential destruction permit deleting retained journals?
faqs.a: No. The separate journal-retention duties continue.

articles.keyword: Utah notarial advertising in another language
articles.title: Utah notarial advertising in another language
articles.description: Apply the notice, translation and professional-role limits to a local advertisement.
articles.h1: Utah notarial advertising in another language
articles.lede: A bilingual service advertisement must convey the notary's permitted role accurately.

sections.heading: Identify the advertisement
sections.body: A Utah notary who is not an attorney prepares a Spanish-language advertisement offering appointments. The chapter requires a conspicuous notice in English and in the advertisement's language concerning the notary's nonattorney status and inability to provide legal advice, with the applicable fees. The particular medium also matters because the code addresses substantially communicating the message in radio and television advertising.

sections.heading: Avoid a misleading translation
sections.body: The statute prohibits a literal translation of notary public into a term that implies the person is an attorney. The notary should examine the meaning the term conveys to the intended audience. A fluent translation that suggests broader professional authority would create the problem the provision addresses even if the English title looks familiar to the advertiser.

sections.heading: Keep the appointment within the role
sections.body: At a resulting appointment, a customer asks which immigration form will obtain a benefit. The nonattorney notary cannot supply legal advice, including immigration advice. Describing the available notarial procedures does not grant authority to select a customer's legal strategy. The chapter also contains a separate fee restriction concerning completion of immigration forms, subject to its licensed-attorney exception.

sections.heading: Separate official office from promotion
sections.body: The code also restricts use of the official title or seal to promote a product, service, contest or offering. Review a proposed campaign with that broader rule in view, along with the specific advertising notice. A lawful appointment ultimately still requires appropriate identity, appearance, act procedure and a truthful certificate, regardless of the language used in the advertisement.

faqs.q: Can a nonattorney notary advise on an immigration legal strategy?
faqs.a: The chapter prohibits nonattorney legal advice, including immigration advice.

faqs.q: Is an English-only notice sufficient for a non-English advertisement?
faqs.a: The stated notice requirement calls for English and the language used in the advertisement.

articles.keyword: Explaining Utah fees at a mobile appointment
articles.title: Explaining Utah fees at a mobile appointment
articles.description: Distinguish the authorized fee units from an agreed mileage charge.
articles.h1: Explaining Utah fees at a mobile appointment
articles.lede: Utah sets different fee units for different acts and conditions a separate travel charge.

sections.heading: Identify the acts and fee units
sections.body: A mobile customer requests an acknowledgment of two signatures and an eligible copy certification of several pages. The ordinary statutory ceilings use per-signature units for acknowledgments and per-page units for copy certification. A separate oath without a signature has its own per-person unit. Counting documents alone can therefore fail to match the authorized fee categories.

sections.heading: Discuss mileage before the trip
sections.body: The code permits a travel charge within the applicable approved federal mileage-rate limit. The notary explains that this is separate from the notarial fee and that the law neither specifies nor mandates the travel charge, then obtains advance agreement. Announcing a previously undisclosed travel charge after the appointment does not follow that agreed-travel structure.

sections.heading: Make the fee schedule available
sections.body: The chapter requires an English-language schedule of authorized fees and permits an additional schedule in another language. A clear schedule helps the notary identify what service is being charged and apply the correct unit. A customer's willingness to pay a premium does not enlarge a statutory ceiling for the notarial act itself.

sections.heading: Check the remote provision separately
sections.body: A certified remote notary uses the separate remote per-item ceiling when that provision applies. Remote identity checks, required recording and secure journal storage remain obligations of the process. Distinguish those remote rules from an in-person mobile trip and its separately explained mileage charge so the appointment description, fee calculation and certificate reflect the actual service.

faqs.q: Is the travel charge mandatory?
faqs.a: The code requires explaining that the travel charge is separate and neither specified nor mandated by law.

faqs.q: Are ordinary copy-certification fees counted per signature?
faqs.a: The ordinary copy-certification ceiling is per page.
